nodes.summary: Let $\iota$ and $F$ be finite, and view functions $\iota \to F$ as words with the Hamming distance. For a finite set $A$ of words and $t \in \mathbb{N}$, the $t$-expansion of $A$ is the set of words at Hamming distance at most $t$ from some element of $A$, that is, the union over $a \in A$ of the closed Hamming balls of radius $t$ about $a$.
nodes.title: Hamming expansion

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number. For points $x, y \in \{0,1\}^n$, write $d_H(x, y)$ for the Hamming distance between them, the number of coordinates in which they differ. For a set $S \subseteq \{0,1\}^n$ and a natural number $t$, write $S_t$ for the set of points $x \in \{0,1\}^n$ with $d_H(x, s) \le t$ for some $s \in S$.
